intended: The mid-passage line tallies the timings over the runs that stayed on the issued route, and the clause beside it records that about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route. The claim is about delivery time on the runs the routing change was rolled out to, so the population is every run dispatched and the minute figures describe roughly five sixths of it. A run leaves the issued route when it meets a blockage or a diversion, which is exactly what makes a run come in long, so an average taken over the runs that stayed on it sits below the figure for all runs dispatched, and the reductions of 8, 5, 9 and 6 minutes are consistent with no reduction at all. The four groups run out of Kettleby Wharf, Stanmoor Yard, Devening Cross and Harkaway Point across four different months, and the same sixth drops out at each depot, so the spread over depots, vehicle types and months does nothing to close the gap.
reported: The timings are selected on the outcome-relevant behaviour: "Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route." The ~17% of runs that abandoned the new route - exactly the ones where it presumably worked badly - are dropped from the after period, so the 5-9 minute improvement is measured on a survivor subset.

Roughly 17 percent of runs at every depot are excluded from the averages, and route deviations are exactly the runs likely to be slow, so the 5-9 minute improvement is measured on a self-selected compliant subset rather than on delivery runs generally.

intended: All four cohorts are starter signups from Norway via webinar inside one March window, so the trial fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: the free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and a thirty-day trial leaves users still inside their trial at week two. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort here signed up on that trial, so the policy change reaches all four. Each cohort is compared against itself a month earlier, when the seven-day trial still applied, so the longer trial and the onboarding email moved together and the 3 to 6 point lifts cannot be attributed to the email. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the retention figures covering every signup, so the trial length is the whole of the defect.
reported: A rival cause hit every cohort: "The free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and every cohort here signed up on that trial." Under the old ~7-8 day trial, week two fell after the trial expired; under a 30-day trial week two is still inside it, which alone would lift week-two retention regardless of the email.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and the clause beside it records that about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile. The claim is about board defects on the run, so the population is every board built on it and the defect figures describe nine tenths of that. Boards that take a pass on the old profile are the ones routed off the normal flow, and the extra handling and the extra heat cycle raise a board's defect risk on their own, so a rate built on the untouched boards alone sits below the run's own rate and the drops of 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent are consistent with defect production holding flat. The four runs sit on the Aspen, Kestrel, Larkspur and Meridian lines across four different months, and the same tenth falls outside the tally on each, so the spread over lines, board families and months does nothing to close the gap.
reported: The defect rates are computed on a filtered subset: "Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." Roughly a tenth of each run is excluded from the new-profile figure while the prior-month baseline is the whole line, so the 4-7 percent drop compares a narrower, self-selected population against a broader one.

intended: All four cohorts are 40 Fenwick users on Corvid 7 phones inside one March, so the single weather fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: outdoor temperature in each cohort's city fell ten degrees from the month before, which lowers resting heart rate on its own. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort sleeping in unconditioned rooms open to outside air, so the cooling reaches every user whose heart rate was read. Each cohort is compared against itself in February, when the nights were warmer, rather than against an unenrolled cohort in the same month, so the cooling and the app arrived together and the 3 to 6 bpm drops cannot be attributed to the app. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the readings covering every enrolled user, so nothing further is wrong with the item.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: 'Outdoor temperature in each cohort's city fell ten degrees from the month before, and every cohort slept in unconditioned rooms open to outside air.' A ten-degree cooling of the sleeping environment plausibly lowers resting heart rate on its own across all four cohorts, so the 3-6 bpm drops are not attributable to the app.
